raw_response:
I will keep it simple and steady this year. I am 67, so I do not want to chase risky cash crops or anything that needs too much fine management. In Quzhou County, the land, water, and weather fit the usual wheat-maize rotation best, and I already understand that system well. So I will keep one piece of land in winter wheat first, then plant summer maize right after wheat harvest. That gives me food grain, stable yield, and work I can still handle. I will use improved seed instead of old saved seed, because I want more even emergence and fewer problems, but I will not choose something too expensive or unfamiliar. For field work, I will keep fertilizer moderate, irrigate at the key stages, watch disease and insects, and spray only when needed. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and saves labor for me.
